title: Customize Claude Code with mods
summary: Claude Code now supports mods—small TypeScript functions that customize behavior, appearance, and features. They can run before, after, or instead of standard operations (redacting secrets, rewriting tool calls, managing permissions), stack from multiple authors, and can be restricted by admins via security defaults.

title: Giving companies more control over their AI agents, with NVIDIA
summary: Claude Managed Agents integrates with NVIDIA's Open Agent Safety Platform, holding credentials in a separate vault and enforcing policies outside the model. Mathematical proofs confirm access limits and audit trails track all agent actions, critical as agents gain broader access to proprietary systems and data.

title: How Anthropic's sales team rebuilt inbound with Claude Managed Agents
summary: Anthropic deployed Claude Managed Agents to handle inbound buying questions about pricing, security, and plans, handling thousands of daily conversations. The agent reduces deal close time by five days and boosts closer productivity 2.5x, freeing reps for strategic work.

title: Claude for Government is now generally available
summary: Claude for Government has moved from public beta to GA for federal and state agencies, operating in a FedRAMP High authorized environment. It offers usage-based pricing with hard spending caps and department-level admin controls, keeps conversation history local on agency devices, and requires two-person approval for sensitive operations with full audit logging.

title: Coding sessions are longer and use more context. Claude Opus 5.5 is built with that in mind.
summary: Claude Opus 5.5 is optimized for extended, context-heavy coding sessions with 40% lower token costs than Opus 5 and 60% cheaper cached-token pricing. The model delivers 30% faster output, 50% fewer cache misses, and requires fewer turns on complex tasks as context usage has grown 2.6x.

title: Claude Tag now supports personal connectors in channels
summary: Claude Tag Slack integration now lets users add personal connectors like calendar, drive, and CRM alongside shared channel connectors, with optional review mode and sensitivity screening. Access logs to the individual user's account rather than the channel service account, while unattended operations continue using shared connectors.
